# ASVS 5.0.0 L2: V6 Authentication

<!-- Generated by `pnpm security:asvs --write` from the YAML file next to this one. Do not edit by hand. -->

> Self-assessment against OWASP ASVS 5.0.0, Level 2, chapter V6 Authentication: not yet assessed by a person. The entries below are the working state, filled in with tests and code pointers; the maintainer's first pass and second pass are still to come. This is not a certification, and no independent party has reviewed it. OWASP does not certify projects.

Status: **in progress**. 18 pass, 4 n/a, 13 fail.

| **6.1.1** Verify that application documentation defines how controls such as rate limiting, anti-automation, and adaptive response, are used to defend against attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force. The documentation must make clear how these controls are configured and prevent malicious account lockout. | L1 | fail |  | Not met. Rate limiting is described (architecture.md, ADR-0008, route notes) but no document says how login brute force and credential stuffing are defended, how the controls are configured (the rateLimits setting) and how malicious lockout is avoided. Tracked in #9006. |
| **6.1.2** Verify that a list of context-specific words is documented in order to prevent their use in passwords. No list of context-specific words is documented and none is checked (see 6.2.11). Own issue #9106. |

Tracked in #9006. |

Own issue #9110. |

| **6.3.3** Verify that either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms, must be used in order to access the application. For L3, one of the factors must be a hardware-based authentication mechanism which provides compromise and impersonation resistance against phishing attacks while verifying the intent to authenticate by requiring a user-initiated action (such as a button press on a FIDO hardware key or a mobile phone). Relaxing any of the considerations in this requirement requires a fully documented rationale and a comprehensive set of mitigating controls. | L2 | fail |  | Not met (code gap). Local login is a password alone; there is no multi-factor option and no written rationale with mitigating controls. An OIDC provider may enforce MFA, but nothing requires it. Own issue #9107. |
| **6.3.4** Verify that, if the application includes multiple authentication pathways, there are no undocumented pathways and that security controls and authentication strength are enforced consistently. | L2 | fail |  | Not met. Enforcement is fairly uniform (all authentication routes are strictly rate limited, deny by default, PATs cannot reach session-only routes) but the pathways are not documented together, so "no undocumented pathways" cannot be shown (6.1.3). Tracked in #9006. |

| **6.8.1** Verify that, if the application supports multiple identity providers (IdPs), the user's identity cannot be spoofed via another supported identity provider (eg. by using the same user identifier). The standard mitigation would be for the application to register and identify the user using a combination of the IdP ID (serving as a namespace) and the user's ID in the IdP. | L2 | fail |  | Not met (code gap). Identities are keyed by (provider, subject), the standard mitigation (unique index; tested). But a first sign-in links to an existing account with the same verified email address, so a provider that asserts someone else's address as verified can take over that account; the README says to list only providers that verify addresses. A per-provider trust setting for linking would close it. Own issue #9109. |
